mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on (a) Team A's possession FOR being above its own long-run mean and (b) Team B's corner_kicks AGAINST being above the competition context mean. Both conditions must hold simultaneously — neither alone is sufficient.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team A corner_kicks FOR rises when both conditions are met, and the joint effect exceeds the sum of each single-condition effect.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's corner-kick production is jointly conditioned on both its own possession dominance and the opponent's (Team B's) corner-kick concession rate: when Team A holds elevated possession AND faces a side that concedes above-average corners, Team A's corner output rises beyond what either dimension alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) from two different teams to be evaluated jointly. It is not reducible to one observable with one coarse band — it is a genuine two-observable, cross-team interaction.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compare Team A's corner_kicks FOR FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF split, conditioned on whether Team B's possession FOR is below the competition context mean (indicating Team B typically cedes possession). The within-match half-level split is the key structural element.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's possession FOR is suppressed relative to competition context, Team A's ratio of first-half corners to second-half corners rises (corners are less back-loaded) compared to matches where Team B holds more possession.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's first-half corner production relative to its second-half corner production shifts depending on Team B's possession tendency: when Team B typically concedes high possession (i.e., plays low-block), Team A's corner generation is more evenly distributed across halves rather than back-loaded.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match half-level split (first half vs second half corner distribution) conditioned on a cross-team possession dimension — requiring two distinct observables across two teams and a half-resolution split. Not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on (a) Team A's shots_on_target AGAINST being below competition context mean and (b) Team A's possession FOR being above competition context mean. Evaluate Team B's shots_on_target FOR under this joint condition versus either condition alone.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's shots_on_target FOR is more suppressed under the joint condition than under either single condition, indicating a compounding cross-observable interaction.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shots-on-target production is jointly suppressed when Team A's shots-on-target allowed is low AND Team A's possession dominance is high: the combination of a possession-heavy opponent that also concedes few shots on target creates a compounding suppression on Team B's attacking output.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires two distinct observables (shots_on_target and possession) evaluated jointly across both teams. Not a single-observable mirror or a single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on (a) Team B's fouls FOR being above competition context mean and (b) Team A's possession FOR being above competition context mean. Evaluate Team B's cards_2h FOR under this joint condition versus each single condition.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's cards_2h FOR rises more steeply under the joint condition (high fouls AND facing high-possession opponent) than under either condition alone, indicating a non-additive interaction between foul tendency and possession pressure.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's second-half card accumulation (cards_2h) is jointly related to both Team B's foul rate FOR and Team A's possession dominance: when Team B commits fouls at an elevated rate against a possession-heavy Team A, second-half card accumulation for Team B rises beyond what either foul rate or possession differential alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Involves three distinct observables (cards_2h, fouls, possession) across two teams, with a within-match period restriction (second half). Not reducible to any single-observable mirror or single-band split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compare Team A's goals FOR FIRST_HALF vs SECOND_HALF ratio, conditioned on whether Team B's fouls FOR is above the competition context mean. The within-match half-level split in goals is the key structural element, conditioned on an opponent's foul-rate dimension.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B's fouls FOR exceeds the competition context mean, Team A's second-half goals FOR rises relative to first-half goals FOR — the ratio of second-half to first-half goals for Team A is higher in high-foul-opponent contexts than in low-foul-opponent contexts.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goal scoring rate in the second half relative to the first half is asymmetrically related to Team B's defensive foul rate: when Team B commits fouls at a high rate (disrupting Team A's build-up), Team A's goals shift toward the second half rather than being evenly distributed, suggesting a threshold-like adaptation effect across halves.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: Requires a within-match half-level split on goals conditioned on a cross-team foul-rate dimension — two distinct observables (goals and fouls) across two teams with half-resolution. Not a single-observable mirror or single-band split.
